summary:
1 take my red crayon in my lec (see what I mean?). I take my red crayon in my right paw to write you a thank you note for sending me BEYOND CONTROL Although I have not as yet read it, I can see it is a wonderful book and am enjoying looking forward to reading it later when I am not so busy. Generally, I do not read science fiction stories, as they deal with rocket ships and blast pistols and other escape trash, but because you sent me the book free I will try to get through it as best I can. When I am finished I will write you saying I liked it whether I did or not, because that is what you are supposed to do. And I always do what is right, because, as Harlan remarked recently in his column, I am a highly ethical and moral and good person (that is, Har remarked this regarding himself, not me. But I digress). 

Why am I so busy, you may ask. Well, here is why, in order of descending merit ( one ) Tessa and I got married a couple of days ago, and I am frantically running about—on all fours, I guess—trying to cover the check I wrote the minister so it won’t bounce (the check, not the minister). 

(two ) I sold my new novel, FLOW MY TEARS, THE POLICEMAN SAID to Doubleday. They received the MS in mid­ February and took until now to decide. So unable to stand the strain I began another novel, A SCANNER DARKLY. (three ) Doubleday this week bought A SCANNER DARKLY as well. So I sold two (2) novels to Doubleday (Double­ day) in one (one) month.
